record.title: An energy-aware model router reports a measured accuracy–energy tradeoff across seven benchmarks
record.summary: A September 2026 arXiv paper evaluates a learned router that selects among nine open-weight models using accuracy, latency, power and GPU-energy signals. On a held-out replay set of 913 questions across seven benchmarks, the authors report UniRoute accuracy of 0.618 at 2,192.2 J per answer and a KL-GRPO checkpoint at accuracy 0.609 and 1,691.9 J, about 23% lower answer energy. They describe a phase transition near 60% accuracy. The measurements use A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs and GPU energy; the headline comparison does not include router energy, which is discussed separately. This is a paper-reported result for a local-serving regime, not independent reproduction or production deployment evidence.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: In the paper’s held-out replay evaluation of 913 questions across seven benchmarks on nine open-weight models using A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs, UniRoute is reported at accuracy 0.618 and 2,192.2 J per answer, while KL-GRPO step 1500 is reported at 0.609 and 1,691.9 J per answer (about 23% lower). The paper reports a phase transition near 60% accuracy. Headline energy is GPU answer energy and does not include router energy; this is not a measurement of total facility energy or a production deployment.

evidence_gaps.description: Net energy savings after including router inference and scheduling overhead are not established by the headline comparison.
The reported accuracy and energy points have not been independently reproduced.
Production serving and transfer across hardware/model pools are untested in the reviewed evidence.

brief.importance_rationale: If replicated in local serving, a roughly 23% reduction in measured GPU answer energy at a small accuracy decrease could materially affect inference cost and energy use. A 5 reflects quantified relevance within the tested model pool and hardware, limited by replay-only evaluation and exclusion of router energy from the headline comparison.
limitations: Energy comparison is GPU answer energy measured with idle subtraction; it does not represent total system/facility energy.
Router overhead is not included in the headline comparison, though discussed separately; net savings after routing overhead are not established by the headline values.
Answers are replayed from tournament logs, not sampled stochastically during evaluation.
The evaluation uses a specific nine-model pool and A100-SXM4-80GB hardware; transfer to other model pools and serving stacks is unknown.
No independent reproduction or production deployment was inspected.

technical.claimed_result: Table 2 reports UniRoute accuracy 0.618 at 2,192.2 J/answer and KL-GRPO step 1500 accuracy 0.609 at 1,691.9 J/answer on the 913-question held-out replay set across seven benchmarks.
technical.demonstrated_result: No independent reproduction is recorded; values are author-reported from replayed tournament answers.
technical.implementation_status: Evaluation on local A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs; no production deployment result inspected.
technical.mechanism: A learned router selects among nine open-weight models using offline correctness, latency, power and GPU-energy measurements; training uses an energy-aware reward.
technical.regime: 913 held-out replay questions, seven benchmarks, nine open-weight models, A100-SXM4-80GB GPUs, 200 ms NVML sampling and idle-subtracted GPU energy.
technical.reproducibility: This activation inspected the paper HTML and reported tables; it did not execute the released artifact or independently reproduce results.
technical.strongest_baseline: UniRoute Table 2 row compared with KL-GRPO step 1500; the latter has slightly lower accuracy and about 23% lower reported answer GPU energy.

brief.title: An energy-aware model router reports a measured accuracy–energy tradeoff across seven benchmarks
brief.why_it_matters: The work gives a concrete energy–quality operating point for routing among open-weight models and makes the omitted router overhead visible as a boundary on the headline comparison. Energy-aware serving decisions may change near an accuracy target, but these GPU-only replay measurements do not establish total facility energy or deployed savings.
